**Paid pulse and recharge:** each successful 12-second directional pulse spends exactly25 charge points from one eligible reserve cell. Selection checks diver first, then the controlled craft hold; within each hold it sorts eligible item IDs lexicographically, independently of array order. It requires one cell with at least25 points. Locker, buoy and uncontrolled craft cells do not pay for field use, and residual charges do not pool. The prior tool, active-pulse and clipped-ray/boundary checks precede every mutation. Feedback gives cost, selected container and remaining cell charge. Sound cue/origin semantics remain unchanged. Depleted cells do not gate quiet movement, cover or retreat.

The explicit `recharge-cells` command uses the restored bench's complete local fabrication container set and needs no vessel. It changes depleted eligible cell charges to100 plus ordinary feedback, without advancing time or changing identities, vessel health/power/air, source stock or maintenance. Away/unrestored/no-cell/full-cell cases refuse. A healthy empty vessel battery remains empty after this action; physical local reserve/service remains the separate recovery action.

**Local transactions:** the side-effect-free cradle helper retains the original support centres/radii: workshop `DART_BUILD_POSE` with restored workshop and distance<12; pod `(0,-1,8)` with distance<12 and its prior service requirements. It returns the actual site and excludes berthed craft/that craft's berth transaction. Craft cargo eligibility additionally requires the player to be at that matching bench. Crafting uses diver, accessible site locker, accessible deployed buoy and only matching supported cradle holds. Count, check and spend use `fabricationContainers`; central `containerAccessible` supplies the same bench-to-cradle reach to individual and bulk transfers. Existing controlled/local hold access outside benches is retained. Disabled local cargo is accessible without a service grant.

Consistency correction within the assigned access rules: the unrestored workshop's locked locker can no longer fund its own restoration. Carry the repair ingredients or use the local deployed buoy. Recipe prerequisites are unchanged. Both staged preparation scenarios demonstrate this with early meals and unchanged bundle sizes/capacities; no cross-path blocker remains.

`store-materials { from, to }` requires two distinct, accessible, non-equipment containers. It recomputes the shared preview and moves the entire eligible set of whole public stacks drawn from the eight MATERIALS IDs, or refuses atomically for no eligible stacks/insufficient space. Only `containerId` changes; ID, kind, quantity, provenance and sequence remain intact. Same-kind destination stacks are not merged. Meals, cells, tools, buoy, module items and fitted/installed items are excluded. Success reports actual material quantities, destination and CU. Individual transfer refuses an installed reference with remove-first guidance.

**Removable reward:** `dart_acoustic_trim` is the exact item/recipe ID and “Dart acoustic trim” the label. Quantity1, public provenance, null charge, fitted:null,2 CU. Its once-only restored-workshop recipe costs2 conductive crust +2 buoyant resin, requires `dart_base`, and uses the existing C04 `bp_canopy_reinforcement`. Output capacity is checked after spending on a detached draft, before committing. It consumes only half the retained first4+4 Canopy return and gates no pressure/story capability.

`install-module { vehicleId, itemId }` moves the same accessible item into an owned Dart hold if needed and appends its instance ID to the existing modules array. The hold continues to count its2 CU. It checks local supported access, unoccupied/unberthed hull, no active recovery/berth transaction, socket vacancy, intact item, duplicate kind/reference and relocation capacity before mutation. An item already in a full hold needs no additional capacity. There are two small-craft sockets; this M1 kind fits Dart only and at most once.

`remove-module { vehicleId, itemId }` detaches only the reference and leaves the identical2 CU item in that hold. Normal removal uses supported local access. The disabled exterior-collar exception additionally requires retained service tool + Bobbin, empty/unberthed hull, distance<7, personal suit depth, actual capsule clearance and no active recovery/berth transaction. It neither remotely detaches nor repairs/charges. Existing salvage still needs an empty hold and no installed references; it cannot delete a module. Remove→transfer→salvage returns only the unchanged6/3/2 frame investment and the existing bound-patch allocation. The same module reinstalls after rebuilding, without an ingredient refund or duplicate vessel.

Only valid installed trim changes the controlled Dart's target speeds: quiet3→4.2 m/s, normal8 unchanged, boost11→9. Existing quiet-before-sprint speed precedence, acceleration, collision, depth, loudness and drain per second remain. Tests also preserve the existing combined quiet+sprint drain behavior. Quiet power per distance becomes3/4.2 of baseline (about28.6% less) at steady target speed; boost pays the same drain per second while travelling more slowly. Normal cruise remains audible; no threat threshold or noise immunity changed. Uninstalled cargo grants no effect. Disable, patch, service, tow, berth/launch and save/reload retain the reference and item. Carried trim is excluded from ordinary incapacity cache recreation, just like the reusable buoy; its original ID survives.
